label: Confirmed Cases (2026 DRC + Uganda + France)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / WHO / Al Jazeera — 5–7 August 2026
contestNote: DRC: 4,053 confirmed across 53 health zones in 5 provinces (Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo) as of 5 August, published 6-7 August. Uganda's outbreak was declared officially over 28 July 2026 (20 confirmed, 18 recoveries, 2 deaths). France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. WHO estimates true DRC case count could be up to 4x higher than reported given 33 of 49 previously-affected zones still show active transmission and community mistrust limits detection.
delta: +3,674 DRC since 5 June (381 → 4,053); Uganda outbreak closed 28 July
deltaNote: DRC confirmed cases roughly tenfold since early June: 400 (June 5) → 2,011 (July 15) → 2,473 (July 21) → 3,605 (July 30) → 4,053 (August 5). This is now the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC history and the second-largest ever recorded worldwide, behind only the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic (28,616 cases).

source: DRC Ministry of Health / WHO DON614 — 5–7 August 2026
deltaNote: Epidemiological week 30 (through 26 July) recorded the highest weekly total yet: 567 new cases and 296 deaths. 694 patients currently hospitalized in isolation in DRC. Africa CDC director Jean Kaseya has warned this could become 'the worst outbreak the world has ever documented' without immediate funding and vaccine deployment.

label: Deaths (2026 Outbreak)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / WHO — 5–7 August 2026
contestNote: Confirmed deaths: 1,850 DRC + 2 Uganda = 1,852 total as of 5 August. CFR (confirmed): ~45.6% (1,850/4,053 DRC). It took only 67 days for the outbreak to cross the 1,000-death milestone (22 July) versus 142 days for the 2014 West Africa epidemic — the fastest fatal surge in Ebola's recorded history.
deltaNote: DRC confirmed deaths: 64 (June 5) → 754 (July 15) → 1,031 (July 22) → 1,587 (July 30) → 1,850 (August 5). 151 confirmed cases among healthcare workers, 44 deaths (29% CFR among HCWs).

label: Case Fatality Rate (2026 BDBV)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / WHO / CIDRAP — 5–7 August 2026
contestNote: Crude CFR calculated from reported confirmed cases/deaths; WHO's 30 July DON put CFR at 44% (1,587/3,605). CFR has climbed steadily as the outbreak has spread into less-accessible, less-resourced health zones. BDBV historically 25–47% CFR, but this outbreak's crude CFR now exceeds the historical range, likely reflecting under-ascertainment of milder cases as much as true severity.

label: BDBV Vaccine Status — WHO Recommends Ervebo Phase 3 Trial
value: WHO TAG recommends Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) for Phase 3 ring trial (7 Aug 2026)
source: WHO Technical Advisory Group on Candidate Vaccine Prioritization / Gavi — 7 August 2026
contestNote: 7 August: WHO's TAG-CVP recommended prioritizing Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV, licensed for Zaire ebolavirus) for a Phase 3 ring-vaccination trial in DRC to test cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus. Animal data: 3/4 vaccinated primates survived BDBV challenge vs 1/4 controls; a ferret study showed 100% protection with a research-grade formulation vs 0% in controls. WHO cautions efficacy against transmission/infection may be low even if protection against death is achieved. Gavi maintains a 500,000-dose Ervebo stockpile, with doses already deployed to DRC, plus $40M committed from its First Response Fund toward Bundibugyo-specific candidates. Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV Phase 1 trial (launched 13 July) and IAVI's rVSV BDBV remain in earlier-stage human trials.
delta: Reversal of 28 May off-label-use ban — Ervebo now headed to a formal Phase 3 BDBV trial
deltaNote: The 28 May WHO expert panel ruling barred Ervebo use outside research settings; the 7 August TAG-CVP recommendation is the first step toward a structured clinical trial pathway rather than a resumption of off-label ring vaccination.

value: 5 DRC provinces (53 health zones) + Uganda (outbreak closed) + France (recovered) + Germany (treated)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / WHO DON614 — 5–7 August 2026
delta: Expanded from 3 to 5 DRC provinces since June (added Haut-Uélé and Tshopo, 11 July)
deltaNote: Ituri Province: 87-88% of all confirmed cases and deaths, spanning 28 of the 53 affected health zones. North Kivu: 11 zones. South Kivu: 1 zone. Haut-Uélé: 5 zones. Tshopo: 4 zones (both formally added to the epidemic zone 11 July 2026). Active transmission ongoing in 33 of 49 previously-affected health zones as of early August. Uganda's outbreak (Kampala + Wakiso) was declared over 28 July. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains largely inaccessible to response teams.

label: Contact Tracing Coverage (DRC)
value: 17,863 contacts under active follow-up (66-81% by province)
delta: Coverage improved from ~45% (June) but remains uneven by province
deltaNote: WHO reports 17,863 contacts identified under follow-up as of 30 July, with active follow-up rates of 75.5% (Ituri), 74.6% (North Kivu), 80.6% (Haut-Uélé) and 66.2% (Tshopo) — all still below the 90%+ threshold needed for rapid suppression. Uganda's contact-tracing program (668+ monitored at peak) is now closed following the 28 July outbreak-end declaration. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains a contact-tracing dead zone.
